title: Sudan’s ‘Lost Boy’ Becomes US Chess Champion
main_content:
In the middle of the 1980s, thousands of boys from Sudan escaped the country’s civil war by walking. They are the so-called “Lost Boys of Sudan” and they had little time for games.

But one of them did learn a game to help him ignore his hunger in a refugee camp. The game was chess. This boy became an expert.

His name is Majur Juac. Today, Mr. Juac shares his chess skills with students in public and private schools, in chess camps and at other events.


During Sudan’s civil war he was forced out of the country. He fled to Ethiopia with 20,000 other Lost Boys.

They made it to Ethiopia. Then, civil war broke out in that country. Majur Juac and his friends had to flee again. Majur Juac landed in Kenya and lived in a refugee camp. It was there that he taught himself to play chess.

In 2004, Majur Juac arrived in the United States. He continued to play chess. He told the Wall Street Journal that he went to a chess tournament in New York while visiting a friend there. He had only meant to watch the tournament. Instead, he entered it. He finished as tournament champion.

That competition led to the connections that began his life as a chess teacher.

Majur Juac still has a big goal ahead of him. That goal is to become an international chess master.

questions.question: What does Majur Juac do now?
options: A. He participates in international chess championships.
B. He shares his chess skills with students.
C. He works as a professional chess player.
D. He runs a chess academy in Sudan.
questions.answer: B. He shares his chess skills with students.

questions.question: Where did Majur Juac learn to play chess?
options: A. In a chess club in the United States.
B. At a refugee camp in Kenya.
C. Online during his time in Sudan.
D. From a chess master he met in Ethiopia.
questions.answer: B. At a refugee camp in Kenya.
